<reason>A won by making the live comparison easier to decide: platforms already use visible follows, suggestions, and address-book import for growth, so CON’s third-party-data veto functions mainly as an exit barrier. Number-portability lock-in survived as the cleaner market story, and B’s only named alternative was a user-side list export that does not actually transfer the graph. B’s accountability-boundary and harm-or-new-moat dilemma was the strongest negative material, and Cambridge Analytica was a fair warning, but B overextended that scandal into any mandated pipeline and never neutralized the captivity claim. B’s clipped opening also left the voluntary/antitrust alternative underbuilt.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s first rebuttal that follower lists, mutuals, and contact import already traffic in the same ties, so CON’s privacy rule appears only when a user tries to leave; B later confirmed the weaker souvenir-export alternative, which A then used as the closing weigh-up.</best_rebuttal>
